subject: Retention decision tree: examples for requests vs generated outputs
messages:
From: Anna Lee <anna@ledgercorp.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on what Redwood keeps by default (prompts / outputs / streaming tokens)

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this — LedgerCorp's security team is running through the data residency & retention section of our procurement checklist. A couple of concrete items we need clarified for our legal/audit folks:

1) By default what items are retained by Redwood for hosted API requests? Specifically: full user request payload (prompts), streaming token traces, intermediate model outputs (partial replies), and final generated outputs.

2) For streaming responses, do you persist token-level streams anywhere (for debugging/analytics) after the call completes? If so, how long and where?

3) KV cache: if customers use session-based KV caching (e.g., chat contexts stored server-side to support shorter prompts), is that treated as a stored artifact and subject to the same retention horizon?

4) If we need to trigger a customer-sponsored purge (DSR/erasure), what's the end-to-end timeline and evidence we receive that data was removed?

If you can send concrete examples (e.g., "If a user calls the hosted API with a 200-token prompt and receives streaming reply X, Redwood will keep A, B, C for N days") that would help our auditors sign off.

I've attached our standard security questionnaire — the relevant tabs are 4.1/4.2.

Appreciate it,
Anna
Security Operations
LedgerCorp

Attachment: security_questionnaire_ledgercorp.xlsx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lee <anna@ledgercorp.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-25T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on what Redwood keeps by default (prompts / outputs / streaming tokens)

Hi Anna — thanks for the detailed list and for sending the questionnaire. I pulled together a concise decision-tree and examples (attached) to map the most common customer scenarios to what we retain by default and the purge paths. High level upfront:

- Default capture model: we store "request payloads" and "final generated outputs" by default for hosted API customers for a configurable retention window (default: 45 days). This supports analytics, billing, and quality monitoring.
- Prompts vs derivative outputs: prompts (user inputs) are stored as part of the request record; model-generated outputs are stored as the final record. Intermediate or partial outputs emitted during streaming are not persisted as separate permanent objects by default — we reconstruct final outputs from the final response record.
- Streaming tokens: token-level traces are captured in an ephemeral buffer for the duration of the request only. We persist token traces to long-term storage only if the customer has explicitly enabled detailed debug logs or if the request triggered an automatic capture via an error/incident rule.
- KV cache: server-side session KV (used for chat continuity) is treated as a stored artifact. By default KV entries follow the same retention window as other stored request records and are eligible for purge when the customer's retention policy is invoked.

Concrete examples (copied from the attached matrix):
A) Simple non-streaming call (200 token prompt, 120 token final output): we store request record (includes prompt) and final output record; retention = 45 days by default.
B) Streaming call (same sizes) with streaming only: token stream is ephemeral and not stored beyond request unless debug capture is enabled. Final output record stored if request completes successfully; retention = 45 days.
C) Streaming call with error capture: token-level stream and additional debug dump retained for 90 days for incident investigation; this capture path requires either (1) customer opt-in for debug or (2) platform auto-capture triggered by a runtime error.

DSR / erasure process: we honor erasure requests from the account owner for hosted customers. Standard SLA is:
- Acknowledge receipt within 1 business day.
- Execute purge from primary stores within 7 calendar days.
- Delete or mark tombstoned within analytic/long-term stores within 30 calendar days (some downstream backups may take longer to expire; we provide a certificate and evidence of deletion).

Residency note: for EU-region customers we keep primary records in the EU region; backups and long-term analytics follow our cross-region policies (documented in the attached flow diagram).

I've attached: retention_matrix_v1.xlsx and redwood-data-flow-diagram.png.

If helpful, we can run through a few LedgerCorp-specific examples on a quick call.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Anna — quick follow-up on streaming and KV cache details (quoting Neha below).

On 2026-10-25T10:34:00-07:00 Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Streaming tokens: token-level traces are captured in an ephemeral buffer for the duration of the request only. We persist token traces to long-term storage only if the customer has explicitly enabled detailed debug logs or if the request triggered an automatic capture via an error/incident rule.

To add some operational color:
- Ephemeral buffers are held in RAM on the serving host and are never written to durable object storage unless a capture trigger fires.
- When debug capture is enabled, token traces are written to a dedicated debug bucket scoped to the customer and flagged for a longer retention (90d). These buckets are visible to the customer's account admins via the Console; they can request immediate purge.
- KV cache entries are versioned with TTLs tied to the session. If a customer requests erasure, we mark the KV keys tombstoned and evict them on the next compaction (usually within 24-72 hours). We provide a purge token / evidence ID for each KV purge operation that you can include in audit evidence.

Let me know if you want sample API payloads and the exact purge evidence fields — happy to add to the matrix.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Product — Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
